extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for applying restriction/election practice and making double-patenting rejections in U.S. patent prosecution, including special rules for nucleotide sequence claims, provisional rejections, and use of terminal disclaimers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election and fee or petition under 37 CFR 1.129(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must either: (1) elect the invention or inventions to be searched and examined and pay the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(s) for each independent and distinct invention in excess of one which applicant elects; or (2) file a petition under 37 CFR 1.129(b) traversing the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in all restriction/election requirements subject to transition restriction provisions (37 CFR 1.129(b)) mailed after June 8, 1995. Refer applicants to current fee schedule for proper amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund when divided inventions rejoined by linking claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever divided inventions in a transitional application are rejoined because a linking claim is allowable and applicant paid the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(s) for the additional invention, applicant should be notified that he or she may request a refund of the fee paid for that additional invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should notify the applicant of refund availability when rejoin occurs due to allowable linking claim. See MPEP §§ 809, 821.04 and 821.04(a) for related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund when nonelected species embraced by allowable generic claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever claims drawn to an additional species in a transitional application for which applicant paid the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(s) are no longer withdrawn from consideration because they are fully embraced by an allowable generic claim, applicant should be notified that he or she may request a refund of the fee paid for that additional species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of when nonelected species would no longer be withdrawn should follow MPEP §§ 806.04(d), 821.04, and 821.04(a). Examiner should notify applicant of refund option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that distinct nucleotide sequences are independent inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynucleotide molecules defined by their nucleic acid ("nucleotide sequences") that encode different proteins are structurally distinct chemical compounds. These sequences are thus deemed to normally constitute independent and distinct inventions within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 121. Absent evidence to the contrary, each such nucleotide sequence is presumed to represent an independent and distinct invention, subject to a restriction requirement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 121 and 37 CFR 1.141 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has partially waived certain restriction rules to permit a reasonable number of nucleotide sequences to be claimed in one application (see Examination of Patent Applications Containing Nucleotide Sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal limit of ten nucleotide sequences for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been determined that normally ten sequences constitute a reasonable number for examination purposes. Accordingly, in most cases, up to ten independent and distinct nucleotide sequences will be examined in a single application without restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to selected sequences, those patentably indistinct from the selected sequences will also be examined. Sequences encoding the same protein are not considered independent/distinct and will be examined together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptional cases and petitions for additional sequences (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some exceptional cases, the complex nature of the claimed material may necessitate that the reasonable number of sequences to be selected be less than ten. Applicants may petition pursuant to 37 CFR 1.181 for examination of additional nucleotide sequences by providing evidence that the different nucleotide sequences do not cover independent and distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate complexity (e.g., 3D folds) and allow petitions with evidence that sequences are not independent; follow MPEP §1850 for PCT/national-stage considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of alternative claims to >10 individual sequences (example A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications claiming more than ten individual independent and distinct nucleotide sequences in alternative form (e.g., 'an isolated DNA fragment comprising DNA having at least 95% identity to a DNA sequence selected from SEQ ID Nos. 1-1,000') will be subject to a restriction requirement. Only the ten nucleotide sequences selected in response to the requirement and any other claimed restriction sequences which are patentably indistinct therefrom will be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant claims >10 in alternative form, restrict to ten for initial examination; examine selected sequences and those patentably indistinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of combination claims (example B) generally not restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications claiming only a combination of nucleotide sequences (e.g., 'a combination of DNA fragments comprising SEQ ID Nos. 1-1,000') will generally not be subject to a restriction requirement. The presence of one novel and nonobvious sequence within the combination will render the entire combination allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will search the combination until one nucleotide sequence is found to be allowable; order of searching chosen to maximize identification of an allowable sequence; if no individual sequence is allowable, examiner considers whether the combination as a whole renders the claim allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of composition claims reciting different combinations (example C)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications claiming composition claims reciting different combinations of individual nucleotide sequences (e.g., combinations containing at least thirty different DNA fragments selected from SEQ ID Nos. 1-1,000) will be subject to a restriction requirement. Applicants will be required to select one combination for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the selected combination contains ten or fewer sequences, all sequences of the combination will be searched. If the selected combination contains more than ten sequences, follow procedures for combination claims (example B): search until one sequence is allowable, examiner chooses search order to maximize finding an allowable sequence; identification of allowable sequences will cause rejoining/allowance of combinations containing those sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed claim sets (A)-(C) restricted to ten for initial examination
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications containing all three claim sets (A)-(C), the Office will require restriction of the application to ten sequences for initial examination purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on finding of allowable sequences, claims limited to those sequences and combinations containing the allowable sequences and any patentably indistinct sequences will be rejoined and allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder consideration for nonelected claims requiring allowable nucleotide sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonelected claims requiring any allowable nucleotide sequence(s) should be considered for rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §821.04 for rejoinder procedures; examiner should consider rejoinder when nonelected claims become implicated by allowable sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and policy purpose of double patenting doctrine
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctrine of double patenting seeks to prevent the unjustified extension of patent exclusivity beyond the term of a patent. Double patenting results when the right to exclude granted by a first patent is unjustly extended by the grant of a later issued patent or patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus of double patenting analysis is on the claims; requires at least one common inventor and/or common ownership or applicability of joint research agreement exclusions under 35 U.S.C.103(c)(2) and (3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two general types of double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: There are generally two types of double patenting rejections: (1) the 'same invention' statutory double patenting rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 101 and (2) the 'nonstatutory-type' double patenting rejection grounded in judicially created public policy (obviousness-type double patenting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonstatutory double patenting includes rejections based on one-way or two-way determinations of obviousness; rare, fact-specific non-usual obviousness-type rejections may occur (In re Schneller).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-checks before entering a double patenting rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether a proper basis exists to enter a double patenting rejection, the examiner must determine: (A) whether a double patenting rejection is prohibited by the third sentence of 35 U.S.C.121; (B) whether a statutory basis exists; and (C) whether a nonstatutory basis exists. Each determination must be made on the basis of all the facts in the application before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Charts I-A, I-B, II-A, and II-B to assist methodology. Domination is distinct from double patenting and alone cannot support a double patenting rejection, though it does not preclude double patenting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory double patenting (35 U.S.C. 101) test
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory double patenting asks: is the same invention being claimed twice? 'Same invention' means identical subject matter. A reliable test is whether a claim in the application could be literally infringed without literally infringing a corresponding claim in the patent; if such an embodiment exists, statutory double patenting does not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may be worded differently yet be identical in scope (e.g., '36 inches' vs '3 feet'). Statutory double patenting cannot be overcome by a terminal disclaimer; it can be overcome by canceling or amending conflicting claims so they are no longer coextensive in scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph use for statutory 'same invention' rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.30 is the heading for statutory (same invention) double patenting rejections. Use form paragraph 8.31 for a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 where the conflicting claim is in an issued patent. Use form paragraph 8.32 for a provisional rejection under 35 U.S.C. 101 where conflicting claim(s) are in a copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examiner notes: 8.31 is only for earlier patents (not copending apps); do not use these for nonstatutory rejections. Add related form paragraphs (e.g., 8.27, 7.15) when appropriate (common ownership, priority issues, or 102/103 type rejections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling provisional nonstatutory obviousness-type double patenting (ODP) rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provisional nonstatutory ODP rejection is the only rejection remaining in the earlier-filed of two pending applications while the later-filed application is rejectable on other grounds, the examiner should withdraw that rejection and permit the earlier-filed application to issue without a terminal disclaimer. If the ODP rejection is the only rejection remaining in the later-filed application while the earlier-filed application is rejectable on other grounds, a terminal disclaimer must be required in the later-filed application before the rejection can be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provisional ODP rejections are the only rejections in both applications, withdraw ODP in the earlier application to permit issuance and require a terminal disclaimer in the later-filed before withdrawal. If both applications filed same day, determine base vs improvement; ODP in base can be withdrawn without terminal disclaimer while improvement cannot. For three conflicting applications, terminal disclaimers must be filed in at least two to link all three.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of terminal disclaimers for statutory double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer cannot be filed to obviate a statutory double patenting rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 101.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statutory DP is the only rejection in an application, examiners should withdraw the rejection and permit the application to issue where appropriate; otherwise follow the provisional rules described for statutory provisional rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejections involving published applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting may exist where a published patent application and an application are filed by the same inventive entity (or related by common inventor/assignee/joint research). Since the published application has not yet issued as a patent, the examiner may make a 'provisional' rejection on the ground of double patenting when the published application has not been abandoned and claims pending therein conflict with claims of the application being examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make provisional double patenting rejections as described for copending applications; ensure the published application is active and not abandoned before making provisional rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A double patenting issue may raise a substantial new question of patentability of a claim of a patent, and thus be addressed in a reexamination proceeding. Double patenting may exist where the reference patent/application and the patent under reexamination are filed by inventive entities with at least one common inventor and/or common owner/assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent under reexamination was granted on or after Dec 10, 2004, double patenting may also exist where inventions resulted from activities undertaken within scope of a joint research agreement pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2) and (3), provided evidence is of record. A DP rejection may NOT be made on this basis if the patent under reexamination issued before Dec 10, 2004. The prior art exclusion under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) cannot be used to overcome an obviousness-type double patenting rejection. See MPEP §2258 and §706.02(l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of double patenting rejections in certain divisional situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a double patenting rejection is not permitted where the claimed subject matter is presented in a divisional application as a result of a restriction requirement made in a parent application under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must consider the third sentence of 35 U.S.C.121 before making a DP rejection; if prohibition applies, DP rejection cannot be made.
